title: Lamed Hebrew Letter (ל): Sound & Words
description: Learn the Hebrew letter Lamed (ל), the tallest Hebrew letter: its [l] sound, its prefix meaning “to” or “for,” words like לֵב (heart), plus practice.

editorialIssues.detail: The letter-sound matching exercise pairs נ with [n]; Nun is not introduced until lesson 14. Beginner scaffolding can be improved separately from the approved source synchronization.

blocks.0: Lamed Hebrew Letter (ל): Sound, Words & Practice

1.tip: Lamed (ל) is the 12th letter in the Hebrew alphabet.

6.tip: יֶלֶד means 'boy', לֶחֶם means 'bread', and לַיְלָה means 'night'.

theory.heading: Meet Lamed
theory.intro: The twelfth letter of the Hebrew alphabet. Lamed makes a plain [l] sound, as in “leaf,” and it is the tallest Hebrew letter: its top stroke rises above the line. At the start of a word, Lamed can also be a prefix meaning “to” or “for,” as in לְדָוִד [le-da-vid], “to David.”
objectives: Recognize Lamed: <bdi class="hebrew" lang="he" dir="rtl">ל</bdi>, the tallest Hebrew letter.
Read Lamed in real words like <bdi class="hebrew" lang="he" dir="rtl">לֵב</bdi> (heart) and <bdi class="hebrew" lang="he" dir="rtl">יֶלֶד</bdi> (boy).

examples.heading: Lamed in real words
examples.intro: See Lamed in two new words, then five reading-practice words. Read each one aloud; the Latin transcriptions are reading aids, not IPA.
